previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, anxiety, and recurrent UTIs was admitted with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain, nausea, and hyperglycemia. She presented with diffuse abdominal tenderness, leukocytosis, hyponatremia, and acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration from poor oral intake. Her pain was managed per protocol with non-narcotic medications, including amitriptyline, sertraline, and lorazepam. She developed transient acidosis and diarrhea, which resolved. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and a renal ultrasound showed no hydronephrosis. Her condition improved with IV fluids, medication adherence, and supportive care. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved labs, and plans to follow up with her primary care provider for diabetes and anemia management.

Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ Intensive care unit (ICU) because of 
your abdominal pain and then found to have what is called 
DIABETIC KETOACIDOSIS (DKA). This is when your sugars are 
uncontrolled and causes changes on your blood levels of 
electrolytes that can be dangerous. This may have been because 
of being dehydrated and also not taking your full insulin doses 
which is very important. 

It is very important that you take your insulin regimen as is 
and follow up closely with your doctor's office closely. ___
